To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the reactions of Ni I(OEiBC)- with a variety of alkyl halides in polar solvents proceed via hydride intermediates; (2) alkene isomerization is a consequence of the hydride mechanism; (3) alkene formation occurs via a dehydrohalogenative pathway; (4) alkene coupling is a minor process in these reactions; (5) the dehydrohalogentation process involves β -hydrido elimination

the Ni I (OEI BC) - reacts with alkyl and aryl halogenides in polar solvents to produce alkane, alkene, and dehydrohalogenated products, with the relative amounts of each depending on solvent and substrate.
the nickel(I) complex reacts with alkyl halides to give alkyl nickel species that undergo dehydrogenation to give olefin products.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the chemistry of nickel(I) complexes.
developing new synthetic routes to novel metal complexes.

the chemistry of the nickel(I)-octaethylisobacteria chlorin anion (Ni I (OEi BC)-) and related complexes of the nickel(I)/nickel(II) redox couple with the tetrapyrrolic macrocycles, porphyrins and chlorins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nickel(I) porphyrin system is a very effective reducing agent for alkyl and aryl halide substrates and that the reaction pathway is dependent on the solvent and on the structure of the substrate.

the reactions of Ni I(OEiBC)- with a variety of organic halides are best explained as proceeding by way of a nonradical nickel(I) mechanism involving alkyl-nickel intermediacy and β -hydrido elimination.
the reactions of NiI(OEIbc)- with alkyl or aryd halides in nonpolar solvents proceed via a radical mechanism and in more polar solvents via a nonradical mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Ni I (OEI BC)- behaves as a mild, nonradical reagent for alkyl and aryl halide reduction, dehydrohalogenatation, and coupling.
the nickel-based mechanism is operative for the reduction of alkyl and aryl halide substrates by the nickel(I) porphyrin anion.

the nickel(I) complex is capable of reducing alkyl halides and of catalyzing the dehydrohalo generation of alkyl and aryl halide substrates, but that the reduction and dehydrohalogena tion processes are not coupled.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Ni I (OE i BC)- system provides a new, nonradical route to alkene formation.
the nickel(I) porphyrin anion is a highly reactive, yet selective, catalyst.
the nickel(II) porphyrin anion, Ni(II)P, is a very effective catalyst for the dehydrohalo-genation of alkyl halides.
